newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Russia's Lebed cautions NATO over expansion plans.
newsitem.headline: Russia's Lebed cautions NATO over expansion plans.

text.p: Russian security chief Alexander Lebed called on NATO on Monday to approach the issue of eastward expansion of the alliance with extreme caution.

Lebed said after talks at NATO headquarters with alliance Secretary-General Javier Solana that security in Europe must serve the interests of all countries. "Every step must be calculated. Take stock, take stock and take stock again," he told reporters.

President Boris Yeltsin's security adviser has been among the most vociferous opponents of plans in the 16-nation alliance to incorporate some former members of the now defunct Soviet-led Warsaw Pact alliance. But his comments on Monday left open the possibility, from his viewpoint, of an arrangement with NATO.

"I came to say let's work together, let's solve the problem... of modernising, reforming NATO, the establishment of special, as we say, relations between Russia and NATO, expressed in an agreement or treaty with legal status and then, further take a decision on expansion or non-expansion," he said.
He said he had new proposals on solving the dispute but did not have time to present them. These would be discussed at a meeting later on Monday with NATO ambassadors.
Asked if he had heard any new initiatives from Solana during his first round of talks, he replied: "Nothing."
